title: Microsoft Purview DLP: act on classification failures in Exchange Online
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft Learn supports the administrator-enabled default, portal toggle, PowerShell command and documented scanning behaviour. It accurately distinguishes the preview documentation from the roadmap's In development status and September target, and keeps unpublished pricing and cloud details qualified.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing
claims.claim: Exchange Online DLP policies can detect and act on classification failures when the classification service cannot fully scan an attachment.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview data loss prevention (DLP) policies for Exchange Online can detect and act on classification failures—cases where the classification service can't fully scan a document.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents this feature as preview.
claims.quote: Configure default protection for classification failures in Data loss prevention for Exchange (preview)

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Classification failure detection is admin-opt-in: the new detection does not apply until an administrator enables it.
claims.quote: By default, these conditions detect only text extraction failures. After you enable classification failure detection, they also detect classification failures such as timeouts, throttling, and other errors.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; rendered controls table
claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal path is Settings > Data loss prevention > Scan failure settings for Exchange > toggle.
claims.quote: from the Microsoft Purview portal, go to Settings on the left navigation menu > Data loss prevention > Scan failure settings for Exchange. In Scan failure settings for Exchange turn on the toggle.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Scope: Rollout; Governance controls; rendered controls table
claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig -DlpErrorHandlingConfig $json in Security & Compliance PowerShell sets classification failure detection.
claims.quote:
Connect to Security & Compliance PowerShell and run the following commands.
Connect-IPPSSession
$json = '{"Classification":{"State":1}}'  # To disable, set State to 0
Set-PolicyConfig -DlpErrorHandlingConfig $json

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The enabling value of $json is the JSON string {"Classification":{"State":1}}.
claims.quote: $json = '{"Classification":{"State":1}}'  # To disable, set State to 0

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Using the same command with Classification.State set to 0 disables detection.
claims.quote:
$json = '{"Classification":{"State":1}}'  # To disable, set State to 0
Set-PolicyConfig -DlpErrorHandlingConfig $json

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft advises allowing up to one hour for synchronisation before validating policy behaviour.
claims.quote: Allow up to one hour for the setting change to synchronize across the service before validating policy behavior.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: This classification failure detection setting applies to Exchange Online only.
claims.quote: This setting applies to Exchange Online only.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Workload
claims.claim: The setting does not affect SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams or Endpoint DLP policies.
claims.quote: It doesn't affect SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, or Endpoint DLP policies.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: By default, Document couldn't be scanned detects text extraction failures, including files that cannot be opened, unsupported formats and password-protected files.
claims.quote: Document couldn't be scanned | Text extraction failures (for example, the file couldn't be opened, the format is unsupported, or the file is password protected).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Document didn't complete scanning also detects only text extraction failures before enabling classification failure detection.
claims.quote: Document didn't complete scanning | Partial text extraction (for example, content exceeded extraction limits).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope: Rules
claims.claim: Enabling detection extends the two existing scan conditions to classification failures such as timeouts, throttling and other errors.
claims.quote: After you enable classification failure detection, they also detect classification failures such as timeouts, throttling, and other errors.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: DocumentScanFailures lets rules take different actions for Timeout, Throttled and Other classification failures.
claims.quote: To take different actions for specific classification failure types—Timeout, Throttled, or Other—use the DocumentScanFailures condition.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Rules
claims.claim: DocumentScanFailures must be combined with Document couldn't be scanned or Document didn't complete scanning using AND.
claims.quote: Combine it with either Document couldn't be scanned or Document didn't complete scanning using AND

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Rules
claims.claim: DocumentScanFailures cannot be used on its own.
claims.quote: DocumentScanFailures can't be used on its own.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing rules using the two conditions might produce more matches after detection is enabled.
claims.quote: If your tenant already has rules that use these conditions, you might see an increase in DLP rule matches after you enable detection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Scan-failure rules detect failures only from classifiers DLP has already evaluated.
claims.quote: Scan-failure rules detect failures only from classifiers that DLP has already evaluated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A classifier failure in a content-detection rule placed after a scan-failure rule can be missed by that scan-failure rule.
claims.quote: If a content-detection rule is placed after a scan-failure rule and its classifier fails, the failure won't be detected.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Content-detection rules should have higher priority than scan-failure rules.
claims.quote: order your rules so that content-detection rules (sensitive information types, exact data matches, and trainable classifiers) have higher priority than scan-failure rules (Timeout, Throttled, Other)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters
claims.claim: The Learn example uses Audit for timeout, throttling and other scan failures.
claims.quote:
4 | Full scan timeout | DocumentIsUnsupported AND DocumentScanFailures = Timeout | Audit
5 | Partial scan throttling | ProcessingLimitExceeded AND DocumentScanFailures = Throttled | Audit
6 | Other scan errors | DocumentIsUnsupported AND DocumentScanFailures = Other | Audit

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The Learn example uses Block for its content rules.
claims.quote:
1 | Detect credit cards | Content contains Credit Card Number | Block
2 | Detect account numbers | Content contains Account Number | Block
3 | Detect EDM match | Content contains EDM SIT | Block

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The resulting actions are specified by the DLP rules rather than a fixed action imposed by the detection toggle.
claims.quote: Actions define what happens as a consequence of a condition being met.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The feature page describes no new identity or permission model.
claims.quote: Searched: "classification failure" Exchange DLP permissions identity per-policy toggle; opened the complete classification-failure-protection page. It gives portal and Security & Compliance PowerShell instructions but describes no new identity or permission model.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Classification failure detection is a tenant-level Exchange Online DLP setting.
claims.quote:
Set-PolicyConfig -DlpErrorHandlingConfig $json
If your tenant already has rules that use these conditions, you might see an increase in DLP rule matches after you enable detection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The feature page names no per-user or per-policy scope for the detection setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Exchange classification failure protection tenant scope per user per policy GCC default disabled message outcome scan failure; "classification failure" Exchange DLP permissions identity per-policy toggle. Opened the feature page; neither per-user nor per-policy scope is stated.
